claim: Syntactically different URLs often identify the same resource; normalising scheme/host case, default ports, trailing slash, fragment and unused query parameters maps them to one key.
steps: Lower-case scheme and host; drop default port; remove fragment; remove the trailing slash consistently; drop query keys known to be unused (tracking keys such as utm_*, fbclid, spm); sort remaining query parameters.
conditions: Applies to items whose URL is the primary identity, e.g. news and blog links.
limitations: Some normalisations change semantics on some servers (fragment-routed AJAX pages, order-sensitive or meaningful query parameters). Cannot detect reprints on other domains.

claim: MinHash signatures estimate Jaccard similarity; LSH banding finds candidate pairs without comparing all pairs.
steps: Hash each shingle with num_perm permutations, keep minima as the signature; estimated Jaccard = fraction of equal signature entries; bucket by bands to find candidates.
conditions: Worth it when pairwise comparison is too slow (large corpora).
limitations: Adds estimation error and a dependency; daily batches here are small, so exact Jaccard is used instead. Recorded as not applicable at the current scale.

claim: Representing each document by its set of n-grams and thresholding the Jaccard index finds approximate (near-duplicate) matches, e.g. reprints with small edits.
steps: Normalise text; build the set of n-grams per document; compare a new document with kept ones; mark as duplicate when Jaccard >= threshold.
conditions: Near-duplicates share most of their wording. Exact Jaccard is affordable for small batches (hundreds of items); MinHash/LSH approximates it at corpus scale.
limitations: Paraphrases and translations share few n-grams and are missed. Word n-grams need whitespace tokenisation, which does not work for Chinese; character n-grams are a local adaptation, not what the paper evaluated. Threshold must be tuned on labelled data.
